source:
# CSV (RFC 4180): the delimited-data grammar — the second
# general-purpose data-format flavor, riding the json flavor's
# methodology (parsanol-rs#531 grammar breadth).
#
# Edition-2 notes: records are right-recursive through the row list
# (no left recursion). Quoted fields admit any byte except a raw
# dquote (dquotes double per RFC 4180 section 2.7); line breaks inside
# quotes are legal RFC — the quoted class includes them. Unquoted
# fields exclude dquote/comma/CR/LF (textdata, extended past 0x7E to
# 0x10FFFF for UTF-8 content). Bare LF is accepted alongside CRLF
# (editors rewrite line endings); a trailing row terminator is
# optional. A trailing comma is a reject (RFC-strict: every comma
# opens another field).

grammar Csv version "1.0.0" edition 2 {
  crlf = %x0D %x0A
  lf = %x0A
  comma = %x2C
  dquote = %x22

  ## file = record *( eol record ) [ eol ]; one record minimum (an
  ## empty document parses as one empty unquoted field).
  file = csv_record *( eol csv_record ) [ eol ]

  ## eol: the RFC wire form is CRLF; bare LF tolerated.
  eol = crlf / lf

  csv_record = ( field *( comma field ) ) as record
  field = ( quoted_field / unquoted_field ) as field

  ## Quoted: dquote, any non-dquote bytes (CR/LF included — RFC allows
  ## line breaks inside quoted fields), or a doubled dquote escape.
  quoted_field = dquote *( %x00-21 / %x23-10FFFF / dquote dquote ) dquote

  ## Unquoted: RFC textdata (no dquote, comma, CR, LF) extended for
  ## multibyte.
  unquoted_field = *( %x20-21 / %x23-2B / %x2D-10FFFF )

  entry main: file

  test {
    accept "a,b,c"
    accept "1,2\r\n3,4"
    accept "1,2\n3,4"
    accept "\"quoted,comma\",plain"
    accept "\"say \"\"hi\"\"\",x"
    accept "single"
    accept "a,b,\r\n,,c"
    accept "name,age\n\"Smith, John\",42\n\"multi\nline\",1"
    accept "\"unicode ünïcödé\",2"
    accept "row with trailing newline\n"
    accept "a,b,\n"
    reject "\"unterminated,x"
    reject "a,\"mix\"ed"
    reject "a,,b\rc"
    reject "a\tb,c"
  }
}
